Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) Chairman Atty. Don Artes convened the Metro Manila Council (MMC) with Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Secretary Vince Dizon, and several Metro Manila mayors to discuss President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.'s directive to clear waterways and mitigate flooding in Greater Metro Manila.

Other topics tackled in the meeting include the MMC's support for the Paleng-QR PH Plus Program of the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) and Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), the adoption of the Infrastructure Audit (AI) Manual of the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG); and coordination and implementation of Waste-to-Energy (WTE) projects of the Department of Energy (DOE) to address waste management and flooding issues.

#PHILIPPINES: TYPHOON FLOODING KILLS 5, STRANDS THOUSANDS IN CENTRAL PHILIPPINES
At least five people have died and hundreds of thousands have been displaced after Typhoon Kalmaegi unleashed torrential rains across central Philippines on Tuesday. 

The island of Cebu was hit hardest, with entire towns submerged and floodwaters sweeping away vehicles and shipping containers.

Cebu City recorded 183mm of rainfall in 24 hours, far exceeding its monthly average, just before the typhoon made landfall. 

Provincial governor Pamela Baricuatro described the situation as “unprecedented,” noting that floodwaters, not winds, posed the greatest threat.

Local disaster officials confirmed the recovery of two children’s bodies in Cebu City, where rescue operations continue amid rising waters.

data.raw_text:
Typhoon Kalmaegi brings heavy flooding in the Philippines' Cebu Province
.
At least one person was killed when Typhoon Kalmaegi hit the central Philippines on Tuesday, the national disaster agency said, as torrential rains, strong winds and storm surges forced tens of thousands to evacuate from their homes.
.
With sustained winds of 150 kph (93 mph) and gusts of up to 205 kph (127 mph) when it made landfall early on Tuesday, Kalmaegi, locally named Tino, is forecast to move across the Visayas islands region and out over the South China Sea by Wednesday.
.
Video and photos from the Philippine Red Cross showed residents being rescued at one of the villages in Cebu City, which was inundated by floodwater due to torrential rains by the typhoon.
.
Tens of thousands of residents were evacuated across the Visayas region, including parts of southern Luzon and northern Mindanao, and one person had died, the national disaster agency reported.
.
Kalmaegi comes as the Philippines, which is hit by an average of 20 tropical storms each year, is recovering from a run of disasters including earthquakes and severe weather events in recent months.
.
#Asia #Typhoon #Kalmaegi #Philippines
